coreFirstPass.originalFront: What is a random measurement error?
coreFirstPass.originalBack: An unpredictable variation causing scatter in repeated measurements.

coreFirstPass.originalFront: What is a systematic error?
coreFirstPass.originalBack: A consistent shift in readings caused by the method or instrument; repeats do not remove it.

coreFirstPass.originalFront: How do you calculate percentage uncertainty?
coreFirstPass.originalBack: percentage uncertainty = absolute uncertainty ÷ measured value × 100%

coreFirstPass.originalFront: For multiplication or division, how are percentage uncertainties combined?
If y = xⁿ, what happens to percentage uncertainty?
coreFirstPass.originalBack: Multiply the percentage uncertainty in x by |n|.

coreFirstPass.originalFront: Accuracy vs precision?
coreFirstPass.originalBack: Accuracy is closeness to the true value; precision is closeness of repeated readings to each other.

coreFirstPass.originalFront: When calculating uncertainty in a quantity proportional to d², how does percentage uncertainty in d contribute?
coreFirstPass.originalBack: Its percentage uncertainty is doubled for the squared factor.

coreFirstPass.originalFront: Name the six SI base units covered by AQA Physics 3.1.
coreFirstPass.originalBack: metre (m), kilogram (kg), second (s), ampere (A), kelvin (K), mole (mol).

coreFirstPass.originalFront: Express the newton (N) using SI base units.
coreFirstPass.originalBack: 1 N = 1 kg m s⁻², from F = ma.

coreFirstPass.originalFront: Express the joule (J) using SI base units.
coreFirstPass.originalBack: 1 J = 1 kg m² s⁻², because work done = force × distance.

coreFirstPass.originalFront: Express the watt (W) using SI base units.
coreFirstPass.originalBack: 1 W = 1 kg m² s⁻³, because power = energy ÷ time.

coreFirstPass.originalFront: Express the pascal (Pa) using SI base units.
coreFirstPass.originalBack: 1 Pa = 1 N m⁻² = 1 kg m⁻¹ s⁻².

coreFirstPass.originalFront: Express the coulomb (C) using SI base units.
coreFirstPass.originalBack: 1 C = 1 A s, because Q = It.

What powers of ten do mega (M) and kilo (k) mean?
What powers of ten do centi (c) and milli (m) mean?
What powers of ten do micro (μ) and nano (n) mean?
What powers of ten do pico (p) and femto (f) mean?

Convert 1 kilowatt-hour into joules.

What does the SI prefix femto (f) mean?
What does the SI prefix tera (T) mean?
What is the SI base unit for amount of substance?
Fill the gap: the base unit of thermodynamic temperature is ____.
How many joules are in one kilowatt-hour?
What is the derived SI unit of resistivity?
What is resolution?
coreFirstPass.originalBack: The smallest change an instrument can distinguish.

coreFirstPass.originalFront: What is repeatability?
coreFirstPass.originalBack: Same result using the same method, equipment and operator.

coreFirstPass.originalFront: What is reproducibility?
coreFirstPass.originalBack: Consistent results when the method is repeated under changed conditions.

coreFirstPass.originalFront: What is precision in measurements?
coreFirstPass.originalBack: How close repeated readings are to one another.

coreFirstPass.originalFront: What is accuracy in measurements?
coreFirstPass.originalBack: How close a measured value is to the true value.

coreFirstPass.originalFront: For quantities multiplied, how do percentage uncertainties combine?
For quantities added, how do absolute uncertainties combine?
For a measured quantity squared, what happens to its percentage uncertainty?
What do error bars usually represent?
coreFirstPass.originalBack: The range of uncertainty around a measured point.

coreFirstPass.originalFront: How is uncertainty in a graph gradient estimated?
coreFirstPass.originalBack: Compare the steepest and shallowest acceptable gradients.

coreFirstPass.originalFront: What is an order of magnitude?
coreFirstPass.originalBack: The nearest power of ten to a quantity.

coreFirstPass.originalFront: How many joules is one electronvolt?
Which base SI unit is used for amount of substance?
What are the base SI units of a newton?
What are the base SI units of a joule?
What is an anomalous reading?
coreFirstPass.originalBack: A result inconsistent with the trend of the other results.

coreFirstPass.originalFront: How does a zero error affect all measurements?
What is a random error's effect on repeated readings?
How can repeating readings reduce random uncertainty?
coreFirstPass.originalBack: Taking a mean reduces its effect.

coreFirstPass.originalFront: Why is a graph through the origin not always justified?
coreFirstPass.originalBack: A systematic offset or real intercept may exist.

coreFirstPass.originalFront: What should an uncertainty normally be rounded to?
What is the approximate percentage uncertainty in a value x?
How are percentage uncertainties combined for a product of measured quantities?
Fill the gap: uncertainty in (A − B) combines the ____ uncertainties.
What is repeatability in measurement?
coreFirstPass.originalBack: Agreement when the same person repeats a method using the same equipment.

coreFirstPass.originalFront: What is reproducibility in measurement?
coreFirstPass.originalBack: Agreement when conditions such as observer or equipment change.

coreFirstPass.originalFront: What is measurement resolution?
coreFirstPass.originalBack: The smallest distinguishable change shown by an instrument.

coreFirstPass.originalFront: What does fractional uncertainty mean?
coreFirstPass.originalBack: Absolute uncertainty divided by the measured value.

coreFirstPass.originalFront: Why does a high-resolution instrument not guarantee accuracy?
coreFirstPass.originalBack: It may still have systematic error.

coreFirstPass.originalFront: What does an order-of-magnitude estimate communicate?
What is the SI base unit for thermodynamic temperature?
Which prefix represents 10⁻¹⁵?
Which prefix represents 10¹²?
What quantity has base units kg m² s⁻³?
What does an uncertainty error bar represent?
coreFirstPass.originalBack: A range of plausible values for the measured quantity.

coreFirstPass.originalFront: Which graph lines estimate uncertainty in a straight-line gradient?
coreFirstPass.originalBack: The steepest and shallowest acceptable lines.

coreFirstPass.originalFront: Which uncertainty type cannot be removed by repeated readings alone?
Why quote an uncertainty to an appropriate number of significant figures?
What does reproducibility require beyond repeatability?
coreFirstPass.originalBack: Different investigators or apparatus under changed conditions.

coreFirstPass.originalFront: For a product or quotient, how do percentage uncertainties combine?
How can uncertainty in a fitted line's y-intercept be estimated?
coreFirstPass.originalBack: Compare best-fit with extreme acceptable line intercepts.

coreFirstPass.originalFront: What is resolution of a digital measuring instrument?
coreFirstPass.originalBack: The smallest displayed change in the reading.

coreFirstPass.originalFront: How can uncertainty from a set of repeated readings be estimated using their range?
coreFirstPass.originalBack: Half the range: (highest reading − lowest reading)/2.

coreFirstPass.originalFront: When quoting a value and its absolute uncertainty, how should their decimal places compare?
coreFirstPass.originalBack: Quote the value to the same decimal place as its absolute uncertainty.

coreFirstPass.originalFront: When is a graph's y-intercept consistent with zero?
coreFirstPass.originalBack: When zero lies within the plausible intercept range from acceptable lines.

explicitGapNotes: Error-bar representation and extreme gradients on an original graph require diagram-based questions, beyond pure text recall.
The selected 75 core measurement cards define orders of magnitude but do not independently evidence unfamiliar quantitative physical estimates.
A later audit must score new uncertainty calculations using the live examiner-style marking, not only flashcard recollection.
Core topic-label coverage does not certify every cross-topic uncertainty task in Physics papers.
